what: MODS_A2 A28 -- the performance round's baseline, on the machine A25, A26, A27 and A28's own two-cycle multiply produced.  A23's baseline is the ISA round's and is NOT replaced: section 3.6's rule is that neither supersedes the other because they measure two different machines.
fmax_method: A12's binary search on the CONSTRAINT with the verdict from post-route WNS; 1/(T-WNS) is reported nowhere.  Measured on the MUL_CYCLES=3 netlist; the adopted MUL_CYCLES=2 netlist closes the same 96.246 MHz constraint at WNS +0.004 against +0.010.
fmax_spread_note: The search was MONOTONIC, unlike A19's: 104.998 failed by 0.423, 100.000 by 0.210, 97.504 by 0.152, and 96.246 and 95.003 both passed.  The implied path delay across the six runs spans 9.947-11.575 ns, a 1.63 ns spread -- wider than A12's +/-0.4 ns and A19's 0.9 ns, because the router optimises to the constraint and stops.
floorplan: none (A27 measured two pblocks; both were slower and neither is adopted)
flags: -march=rv32im_zba_zbb_zbs_zbkb_zicond_zicsr -mabi=ilp32 -O2 -ffreestanding -nostdlib -nostartfiles -fno-common -Wall | dhrystone: -std=gnu89 + upstream no-inline pragma | mul/div: hardware M extension

vs_a25.note: Identical in EVERY counter.  Dhrystone's multi-cycle EX term is 66,000,000 = 2,000,000 x 33: one divide per run and no multiplies, because at -march=rv32imb the compiler strength-reduces Dhrystone's multiply into Zba shift-adds.  Neither A26's clock work nor A28's shorter multiply can touch it.

coremark.iterations_note: 3500, against A23/A25's 2500.  At 96.246 MHz a 2500-iteration run finished in 7.91 s and a 3300-iteration run at MUL=3 in 10.44 s; CoreMark's own run rules require 10 s and the parser refuses less.  RAW CYCLE COUNTS ARE THEREFORE NOT COMPARABLE with A23/A25 -- CoreMark/MHz and IPC are.
coremark.exstall_decomposition: 32,886,000 stall cycles / 3500 iterations = 9,396 per iteration, one per multiply at MUL=2.  A25 measured 46,980,000 / 2500 = 18,792 per iteration, TWO per multiply at MUL=3.  Same 9,396 multiplies, exactly.

counter_agreement.note: MODS_A2 A28 asks for A20's hardware counters and A18's simulation instrument to be reported as a pair FOR THE LAST TIME.  They agree to the count in all eight comparable rows across both regions on the shipped ISA.  From this point the hardware counters are the primary source and the simulation instrument is the cross-check.
